Bible word search with a word-path example

In Chrust, words follow neighbouring cells and can turn corners. Try this small example before exploring the full word-search game.

Try the example

How to find a word

  • Start at the first letter of a name.
  • Move one cell up, down, left or right at a time.
  • Do not move diagonally or skip a cell.
  • A word can turn a corner. Read it from its first letter to its last.

Find three names

NOAH, SHEM, JOEL. Trace the paths in your mind or copy the grid onto paper.

A word-path practice grid
NOSH
HAME
JOEL
Show the answers

Coordinates are row:column, counted from the top-left corner.

  • NOAH: 1:1 → 1:2 → 2:2 → 2:1. Genesis 6:9.
  • SHEM: 1:3 → 1:4 → 2:4 → 2:3. Genesis 5:32.
  • JOEL: 3:1 → 3:2 → 3:3 → 3:4. Joel 1:1.

A different kind of Bible word search

A conventional word search often hides words in straight lines, sometimes diagonally or backwards. This word-path example uses turns and contains no random filler letters. Look for a connected path rather than only a straight row.

After finding the names

Open the answers and look up the Scripture references. Recall where each person appears in the biblical story, not only how the name is spelled. This website example does not save progress in the app.
